audit.title: Cross-Chain Token (CCT) Tutorials

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with process framing — "Before diving into the tutorials, it's important first to understand the overall procedure" — not a self-contained answer. No lead sentence defining CCT or the three-step flow crisply.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Reasonable heading set and 17 bullets, but the measured **1 level skip** (H1 jumps to H3 "Understanding the Procedure") breaks hierarchy, and there is **0 tables** where a mechanism-comparison table would help extraction.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Only 6 numerals, 0 with units; the numbered 3-step procedure is the strongest concrete content. No rate-limit numbers, no supported-network counts despite linking a rate-limits tutorial.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 22 internal links, well-targeted (TokenAdminRegistry API, token-pools, ERC20 concept). Zero external/primary references — acceptable for a hub, but a link to the CCT standard/spec would raise authority.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No crisp CCT definition; "CCT standard" is only linked, never stated. An engine cannot lift a one-sentence answer to "what is a Cross-Chain Token?" from this page.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured **0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no head captured**. Body carries `Last Updated: 2025-05-19` but no machine-readable dateModified. Weakest dimension.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 code blocks — appropriate for an index page, scored neutral, not penalized as a defect.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers lifecycle (deploy → register → configure → rate-limit → multi-network) but uses concept-titled headings, no "how do I" / "vs" / error-phrased sections, no FAQ.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent terminology (CCT, EOA, Smart Account, Burn & Mint). No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a well-linked navigation hub that routes developers to CCT tutorials by tooling (Remix/Hardhat/Foundry) and mechanism (Burn & Mint / Lock & Mint). Its biggest strength is clean cross-linking — 22 internal links organizing the full enablement lifecycle. Its biggest opportunity is that the page never states a liftable definition of what a Cross-Chain Token is, nor contrasts Burn & Mint vs Lock & Mint in a machine-scannable table — the two things engines would most want to lift from this URL. As a hub it is competent, but it forfeits retrievability for the conceptual and decision-oriented queries that would naturally land here.

recommendations.title: Add a Burn & Mint vs Lock & Mint comparison table
recommendations.where: Under `## Tutorials`, above the bullet list.
recommendations.issue: Mechanisms are only named in link text; no contrast: "Register from an EOA (Burn & Mint)… (Lock & Mint)".
recommendations.change: Insert a 2-column table comparing the two mechanisms on: token supply behavior, when to use each, source vs destination handling, and which pool contract applies — each row one liftable sentence.
recommendations.why: "burn and mint vs lock and mint" is a high-frequency decision query; a table lets engines extract *reasons* and cite this page as the canonical answer.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical CCT definition as the first liftable sentence
recommendations.where: Immediately under the H1, before the prerequisites note.
recommendations.issue: Page opens with process framing, no definition; "CCT standard" is only linked.
recommendations.change: Add 1–2 sentences: "A Cross-Chain Token (CCT) is an ERC20-compatible token enabled for CCIP transfers by deploying a token pool and registering its administrator in the TokenAdminRegistry. Enabling a token requires three steps: token deployment, admin registration, and pool deployment/configuration."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a self-contained chunk to lift for "what is a Cross-Chain Token" — currently unanswerable from this URL.

recommendations.title: Fix the heading level skip
recommendations.where: "Understanding the Procedure" and "Key Steps to Keep in Mind" are H3 under an H1.
recommendations.issue: Measured 1 level skip; missing H2 breaks the chunk hierarchy.
recommendations.change: Promote these to H2 (or wrap them under an H2 "## Enabling a token for CCIP").
recommendations.why: Clean hierarchy improves RAG chunk-boundary detection and section retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: Measured 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no machine-readable dates.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `inLanguage: en`, and a self-referential `canonical`. (Verify head — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.)
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and parse reliability.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased headings
recommendations.where: New sub-sections or reworded tutorial labels.
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled headings ("Understanding the Procedure") miss how devs query.
recommendations.change: Add short H2/H3s like "How do I enable my ERC20 token for CCIP?" and "Which mechanism should I use — Burn & Mint or Lock & Mint?" linking to the relevant tutorials.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to the procedure
recommendations.where: "Key Steps" list and the rate-limits bullet.
recommendations.issue: 0 numerals with units; no network or limit specifics.
recommendations.change: Name the current CCT contract version (`v1.6.1`, already referenced), and one-line what rate limits control (capacity/refill rate) with the parameter names.
recommendations.why: Quantitative, versioned specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

antiPatterns: Heading level skip (H1 → H3), breaking chunk hierarchy.
"Image: Image" placeholder — the process diagram carries no alt text or textual equivalent, so its content is invisible to engines; add a text summary of the diagram steps.
No stale-content risk: `Last Updated: 2025-05-19` present in body (though not machine-readable).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this URL is listed in it.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are template/site-level concerns; fixing once in the docs framework propagates across sibling tutorial pages.
As a hub, this page should be internally linked from the CCT concept/overview pages so it wins the canonical-hub position for "CCT tutorials" queries.
